title.source: Section check: People, memory and shared histories
title.back: Section check: People, memory and shared histories

intro.source: 6 questions about Lessons 10–12. Take your time. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you like.
intro.back: 6 questions about Lessons 10–12. No need to rush. You can look back at the lessons and try again as often as you want.

questions.0.question.source: The photo of the covered bridge in Hội An was taken in 2018. What kind of evidence is it?
questions.0.question.back: The photo of the covered bridge in Hội An was taken in 2018. What kind of evidence is that photo?

questions.0.options.0.text.source: A picture of the port in the 1400s
questions.0.options.0.text.back: A picture of the port in the 1400s

questions.0.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. The photo was taken in 2018, hundreds of years after the port began. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.0.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. The photo was taken in 2018, hundreds of years after the port began. Look back at Lesson 10.

questions.0.options.1.text.source: A view of a place that is still there
questions.0.options.1.text.back: A view of a place that still exists

questions.0.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. The photo shows the bridge on one day in 2018. It cannot show the old traders.
questions.0.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. The photo shows the bridge on one day in 2018. The photo cannot show the old traders.

questions.0.options.2.text.source: A record written by an early trader
questions.0.options.2.text.back: A record written by an early trader

questions.0.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. It is a photo, not a written record. And it was taken in 2018. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.0.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. This is a photo, not a written record. The photo was also taken in 2018. Look back at Lesson 10.

questions.1.question.source: UNESCO describes Hội An's shops, homes and quay. What else could help you learn how people saw the town long ago?
questions.1.question.back: UNESCO describes the shops, homes and quay in Hội An. What else could help you find out how people saw the town long ago?

questions.1.options.0.text.source: Old records or objects from that time
questions.1.options.0.text.back: Old records or objects from that time

questions.1.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. Buildings show us a place. Old records and objects could help us hear the views of people who lived there.
questions.1.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. Buildings show us a place. Old records and objects could help us hear the views of people who lived there.

questions.1.options.1.text.source: A newer photo of the covered bridge
questions.1.options.1.text.back: A new photo of the covered bridge

questions.1.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. A new photo shows the bridge today. It cannot show what people thought long ago. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.1.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. A new photo shows the bridge today. That photo cannot show what people thought long ago. Look back at Lesson 10.

questions.1.options.2.text.source: A longer list of the town's buildings
questions.1.options.2.text.back: A longer list of the town's buildings

questions.1.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Buildings tell us about the place, not what each person thought. Look back at Lesson 10.
questions.1.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Buildings tell us about the place, not what each person thought. Look back at Lesson 10.

questions.2.question.source: Which question can the 1976 photo of Borobudur help you answer?
questions.2.question.back: Which question can the 1976 photo of Borobudur help you answer?

questions.2.options.0.text.source: What did the first builders plan?
questions.2.options.0.text.back: What did the first builders plan?

questions.2.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. Borobudur was built in the 700s and 800s. A photo from 1976 cannot show the builders' plans. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.2.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. Borobudur was built in the 700s and 800s. A photo from 1976 cannot show the builders' plans. Look back at Lesson 11.

questions.2.options.1.text.source: Why did the team choose each repair?
questions.2.options.1.text.back: Why did the team choose each repair?

questions.2.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. A photo shows the work, not the reasons for it. Written records or a worker's memories could help. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.2.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. A photo shows the work, not the reasons for it. Written records or a worker's memories could help. Look back at Lesson 11.

questions.2.options.2.text.source: What did the repairs look like?
questions.2.options.2.text.back: What did the repair work look like?

questions.2.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. The photo records one moment of modern conservation work, in 1976.
questions.2.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. The photo records one moment in modern conservation work, in 1976.

questions.3.question.source: The Borobudur team kept its photos, drawings and notes. People can study them later. What is a set of records like this called?
questions.3.question.back: The Borobudur team kept their photos, drawings and notes. People can study them later. What is the name of a set of records like this?

questions.3.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A stupa is a bell-shaped tower on the monument. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.3.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A stupa is a bell-shaped tower on the monument. Look back at Lesson 11.

questions.3.options.1.feedback.source: Yes. An archive keeps records safe. Later, people can compare them and ask why each repair was made.
questions.3.options.1.feedback.back: Yes. An archive keeps records safely. Later, people can compare them and ask why each repair was made.

questions.3.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. Recognition is when a group says something is important. In 2017, UNESCO said this about the archive. Look back at Lesson 11.
questions.3.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. Recognition is when a group states that something is important. In 2017, UNESCO stated this about the archive. Look back at Lesson 11.

questions.4.stimulus.body.source: This is a made-up example. A class makes a small exhibit about the made-up town of Nolbe. Panel 1 has a photo of an old stone well. The class needs to write a credit under the photo.
questions.4.stimulus.body.back: This is a made-up example. A class makes a small exhibition about the made-up town of Nolbe. Panel 1 has a photo of an old stone well. The class needs to write a credit under the photo.

questions.4.question.source: Which line is the best credit for the photo?
questions.4.question.back: Which line is the best credit for the photo?

questions.4.options.0.feedback.source: Yes. A credit says who made the source, when, and where it is kept. Then others can check it.
questions.4.options.0.feedback.back: Yes. A credit states who made the source, when, and where it is kept. With that, other people can check it.

questions.4.options.1.text.source: Every person in Nolbe used this well
questions.4.options.1.text.back: Every person in Nolbe used this well

questions.4.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. This is a claim about the past, and the photo cannot prove it. A credit says who made the source. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.4.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. This is a claim about the past, and the photo cannot prove it. A credit states who made the source. Look back at Lesson 12.

questions.4.options.2.text.source: This is the best photo in our exhibit
questions.4.options.2.text.back: This is the best photo in our exhibition

questions.4.options.2.feedback.source: Not quite. This is an opinion. A credit names who made the source and where it is kept. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.4.options.2.feedback.back: Not quite. This is an opinion. A credit names who made the source and where it is kept. Look back at Lesson 12.

questions.5.question.source: Your two sources do not show what local people thought. What should you do in your exhibit?
questions.5.question.back: Your two sources do not show what local people thought. What should you do in your exhibition?

questions.5.options.0.text.source: Make up what local people said
questions.5.options.0.text.back: Make up what local people said

questions.5.options.0.feedback.source: Not quite. A fair exhibit does not invent evidence. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.5.options.0.feedback.back: Not quite. A fair exhibition does not invent evidence. Look back at Lesson 12.

questions.5.options.1.text.source: Leave the gap out, so it looks complete
questions.5.options.1.text.back: Do not mention the gap, so it looks complete

questions.5.options.1.feedback.source: Not quite. Hiding a gap makes the story look more certain than it is. Look back at Lesson 12.
questions.5.options.1.feedback.back: Not quite. Hiding a gap makes the story look more certain than it really is. Look back at Lesson 12.

questions.5.options.2.text.source: Say that this perspective is missing
questions.5.options.2.text.back: State that this perspective is missing

questions.5.options.2.feedback.source: Yes. A fair account can say, "This source does not tell us." Then visitors know what is still unsure.
questions.5.options.2.feedback.back: Yes. A fair account can say, "This source does not tell us." With that, visitors know what is still not certain.

results.high.source: Well done. You know how places, records and exhibits can tell a history fairly.
results.high.back: Well done. You know how places, records and exhibitions can tell a history fairly.

results.middle.source: Good work. You got many questions right. Look back at the lessons for the ones you missed, and try again if you like.
results.middle.back: Good. You answered many questions correctly. Look back at the lessons for the questions you have not yet answered correctly, and try again if you want.

results.low.source: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 10–12, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
results.low.back: Thank you for trying. Look back at Lessons 10–12, then try again. You can take as long as you need.
